sections.h2: Which Cheboygan County office takes my deed?
sections.html:
Take it to the County Clerk/Register of Deeds in the county building, 870 South Main Street, Room 204, Cheboygan, MI 49721. Letters go to PO Box 70, and the main line is 231-627-8808. In Cheboygan County the clerk and the register of deeds are the same office, so the same counter handles court filings, marriage licenses and land records.

The Register of Deeds side keeps weekday hours that open at 8:30 in the morning and close at half past four, half an hour after the rest of the clerk's office starts. The county closes on a fixed list of holidays that includes Good Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, so a closing planned near those dates needs an earlier recording plan.

sections.h2: What is the Cheboygan County Register of Deeds responsible for?
sections.html:
It is the repository of official real property records for Cheboygan. The office page says any document that affects real property is recorded there, and it lists warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, wills, mortgages and divorces as examples.

After your sale, this is where the chain of title for the house continues. The county website also offers recording packets: a general recording requirements sheet, a warranty deed with recording requirements, a land contract form and a quit claim deed with recording requirements. Pull those sheets before a drafter starts work, because they show the layout the office expects.

  • Payment is accepted by cash, check and debit or credit card.
  • Coins above $5.00 are not accepted.
  • Card payments can be taken by phone for most services.

sections.h2: What should I bring when I take a deed to the Cheboygan County office?
sections.html:
Carry the signed original deed, payment for the fee and transfer tax, and any tax certificate the deed type needs. For a mailed package, add a return envelope and a note with a daytime phone number so staff can reach you about a problem.

  • The original deed with every signature and notary block complete.
  • A stated total value on the deed or an attached affidavit of value.
  • A check, cash or a card for the recording fee and the transfer tax.
  • The treasurer's certification if the deed carries warranty covenants.

The county was set off in 1840 from land that had belonged to Michilimackinac County, and the name Cheboygan comes from the river, though the precise meaning is no longer known. Mackinaw City, Tuscarora Township and the city of Cheboygan each run their own police departments, which is a reminder that most day to day local rules, from building permits to zoning, sit with the city, village or township rather than the county recording office.

sections.h2: How much is the recording fee in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
State law puts the usual price of entering and recording a document at $30.00, with no extra charge for length. MCL 600.2567 also lists $3.00 for each added instrument on a multi-instrument assignment or discharge, $1.00 a page for copies and $5.00 to certify a recorded document.

A charter county may adopt its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm the total with the Cheboygan office before you write the check. Payment is expected on the day the document is left at the counter, with narrow exceptions for electronic filings and government agencies. A short call to 231-627-8808 gets the exact amount.

sections.h2: What will the state and county transfer tax add up to in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
Both taxes run on the full sale price, counted in $500 steps with a partial step counted whole. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a step and MCL 207.525 sets the state rate at $3.75 a step.

The middle row uses $192,500, which is the Census figure for the county's middle-priced home across the five-year survey ending 2024. The deed must print the total value, or carry an affidavit of value. When a sale bundles in a boat or furniture, stating real and personal values apart keeps the tax on the real property only.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a tax certificate in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
A deed carrying warranty promises needs county treasurer certification first. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that the parcel's taxes are paid for the five years ahead of the deed date, plus a statement of any tax liens or titles.

Subsection (6)(e) excuses a quitclaim deed that has no warranty covenants, and subsection (6)(c) excuses a sheriff's deed from a court proceeding. If a deed is presented after March 1 and before the local treasurer has filed the current delinquent tax return, the certificate carries a note that the return was not available, and the register of deeds may not refuse the deed for that reason alone.

sections.h2: What formatting mistakes get a Cheboygan County deed rejected?
sections.html:
Mismatched names, missing addresses and cramped signature blocks cause most trouble. MCL 565.201 sets the rules that every Michigan register of deeds applies.

  • Each signer's name is printed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the acknowledgment.
  • A notary's name is printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Every grantee's address appears on the deed, using the street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The person who drafted it is named, with a workplace address.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed or obscured.

A deed written in another language needs an English translation attached. A returned deed goes back to your drafter for repair.

sections.h2: What should a Cheboygan County seller know about the local housing picture?
sections.html:
Cheboygan County is big, thinly settled and full of seasonal homes. Its 885 square miles split into 715 of land and 170 of water, and the Census Bureau counts 35.8 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 25,793 people, and 30.6% of them are 65 or older. Owners hold 85.6% of homes, the middle rent is $773, and the typical household earns $62,875 (five-year survey ending 2024). The 2020 count found 36.0% of the 17,631 housing units vacant, and the Census lists 74 building permits for 2025. County government was organized in 1853 after a merger with the former Wyandot County.

sections.h2: How do I protect my Cheboygan County property from deed fraud?
sections.html:
Sign up for Property Activity Alert, a service that watches for recordings under your name. The office explains that it cannot stop fraud, but the alert warns an owner early so they can act. Call 231-627-8866 and the staff will enter your name and email address.

This is useful for sellers who keep another parcel in the county, and for anyone who inherited land and has not yet recorded a transfer into their own name.

faqs.q: When can I reach the Cheboygan register of deeds counter?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds window runs Weekdays, opening at 8:30 and closing at half past four. Other clerk services start at 8:00. Closures follow the county holiday list, which includes Good Friday and the day after Thanksgiving.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by card in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash, checks and debit or credit cards all work at the office, and most services can be paid by card over the phone. Coin payments above $5.00 are refused.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed taxed differently in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: A quitclaim deed does not need the treasurer's tax certificate, but transfer tax can still apply if money changes hands. MCL 207.505 exempts deeds that only confirm a title already held, and deeds with consideration under $100.

faqs.q: How is the county transfer tax calculated in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by $0.55. The state tax rounds the same way at $3.75. A $200,000 sale gives 400 steps, so $220 county tax and $1,500 state tax.

faqs.q: Does the Cheboygan office help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. Hire an attorney or the title agent to draft it. The county posts a general recording requirements sheet and sample warranty and quit claim deed layouts that show what the register of deeds expects.
